law_text: A driver commits an offense of aggressive driving if, during any single, continuous period of driving within the course of 1 mile, the driver does all the following, in any sequence: (a) Commits one or more acts of speeding in violation of NRS 484B.363 or 484B.600 [NRS-484B-363-1, NRS-484B-363-2, NRS-484B-600-1a, NRS-484B-600-1b, NRS-484B-600-1c, NRS-484B-600-1e]. (b) Commits two or more of the following acts, in any combination, or commits any of the following acts more than once: (1) Failing to obey an official traffic-control device in violation of NRS 484B.300 [NRS-484B-300-1]. (2) Overtaking and passing another vehicle upon the right by driving off the paved portion of the highway in violation of NRS 484B.210 [NRS-484B-210-3]. (3) Improper or unsafe driving upon a highway that has marked lanes for traffic in violation of NRS 484B.223 [NRS-484B-223-1b, NRS-484B-223-2, NRS-484B-223-3a, NRS-484B-223-3b, NRS-484B-223-3c, NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b]. (4) Following another vehicle too closely in violation of NRS 484B.127 [LVMC-11-12-080-A, NRS-484B-127-2, NRS-484B-127-3]. (5) Failing to yield the right-of-way in violation of any provision of NRS 484B.250 to 484B.267, inclusive [NRS-484B-250-1, NRS-484B-250-2, NRS-484B-250-3, NRS-484B-250-4, NRS-484B-253, NRS-484B-257-1, NRS-484B-257-2, NRS-484B-260, NRS-484B-263, NRS-484B-267-1a, NRS-484B-267-1b, NRS-484B-267-1c, NRS-484B-267-2a, NRS-484B-267-2b, NRS-484B-267-2c, NRS-484B-267-2d, NRS-484B-267-2e, NRS-484B-267-2f]. (c) Creates an immediate hazard, regardless of its duration, to another vehicle or to another person, whether or not the other person is riding in or upon the vehicle of the driver or any other vehicle.

alternatives_and_boundaries: Single continuous driving period and one-mile distance are explicit temporal/spatial boundaries; probe below, at and above one mile where feasible.
One or more qualifying speeding acts, two acts from the listed categories (or one category twice), and immediate hazard are cumulative conditions.
Distinct listed-act alternatives need source-backed cross-law facts; the fixed overtake-right cell may not support every category.
Hazard has no supplied numeric legal threshold.
